A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with shared methods, proofs, experiments and sample images despite substantial rewriting and the SDB-to-ECSI renaming. All 23 pages of v1 and 36 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-to-image translation experiments, including sampler comparisons, trained-model results and conditional-diversity measurements in Tables 2–4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original translation results and adds ImageNet deblurring, controlled AFD validation and additional ablations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The denoiser, preconditioning, controllable sampling SDE, base-distribution perturbation and mixed discretization are retained under the ECSI name. Algorithm 1 changes its branch condition from N >= 2 to i >= 2, a limited correction to the written sampling procedure. The prose in both versions already prescribes deterministic final steps, so this does not establish a newly implemented sampler.

E1.justification: v2 retains Edges-to-Handbags and DIODE depth-to-RGB translation and adds ImageNet uniform and Gaussian deblurring in Table 5. ImageNet also supplies the class-conditioned resampling and color-augmentation experiments validating AFD in Appendix A. The expanded DIODE results concern an existing dataset, rather than newly introduced coverage.

E2.justification: The new deblurring comparison introduces DDRM, DDNM, CDSB and the method labeled 'Pallette' in Table 5, alongside I2SB. The conditional-diversity comparison in Table 4 also replaces the DDBM-checkpoint-plus-DDBM-sampler baseline with DDBM-checkpoint-plus-DBIM-sampler. The former baseline remains illustrated elsewhere in v2, but its membership in this table changes.

E3.justification: The reported sampling minimum time changes from 0.01 to 0.001, and DIODE receives rho = 0.8 instead of the previously general rho = 0.6. Table 4 changes the diversity comparison to common budgets of 5, 10 and 20 NFEs. New protocols include deblurring on 10,000 ImageNet validation images, controlled resampling and 16 augmentations per image for AFD validation, and a 446-image test comparison. These reported changes do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds component ablations for discretization and final-step noise control, quantitative sensitivity to noise magnitude and schedule shape, and qualitative failure analyses for excessive or insufficient noise (Figure 4 and Appendix D). Appendix A adds two controlled validations of AFD. Conversely, v1's complete numerical eta sweep using pretrained DDBM-VP is reduced to the eta = 0.3 row in v2 Table 2, with additional qualitative comparisons elsewhere.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run performance summaries, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Multiple generated outputs for AFD and the newly specified augmentation counts are evaluation samples, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The shared pretrained-sampler scores and original handbag FIDs of 0.89, 0.67 and 0.56 are retained. v2 adds gamma_max = 0.25 results, trained-model DIODE results including FID 3.27 at 20 NFEs, deblurring FIDs of 1.11 for uniform blur and 0.41 for Gaussian blur, and extensive AFD results. v1's DDBM-200-NFE and DBIM-100-NFE rows and most numerical eta-sweep entries disappear. These are added or removed results, rather than demonstrated gains under identical settings.

T1.justification: The principal sampling and denoising results and their proofs are retained through Proposition 4.1 and Appendix B; their reorganization does not constitute new theory. Limited additions include Appendix D's time-reparameterization argument for linear interpolation and Appendix F's derivation of TrigFlow as a special case. The mathematical definition of AFD is unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contribution is recast from stochasticity control and singularity mitigation to unifying stochastic interpolants with endpoint conditioning and preconditioning. The abstract and introduction drop the explicit fivefold acceleration and training-stability emphasis, while the headline empirical scope expands to deblurring. The conclusion also strengthens the diversity claim: modifying the starting distribution is described as required, rather than simply beneficial.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a lossy-compression and data-processing interpretation of base-distribution perturbation, explains AFD's complementarity to FID using controlled examples, and develops noise-dependent failure explanations and tuning guidance in Appendix D. v1's explicit singularity and truncation-error rationale is removed. Task dependence and the quality-versus-diversity tradeoff were already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: Appendix F/Table 9 substantially expands the training documentation beyond v1's two handbag configurations, adding a gamma_max = 0.25 handbag configuration and two DIODE configurations with hardware, batch sizes, learning rates and training times. Budgets are now expressed in epochs rather than iterations, without establishing that existing training runs changed. The architecture and preconditioning details are largely retained, while sampling settings and new evaluation procedures receive additional documentation.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly positions ECSI as an extension of stochastic interpolants combining their flexibility with practical diffusion-bridge components, supported by a new characteristics table and fuller DBIM discussion. It adds connections and citations to data-dependent stochastic interpolants, augmented and inverse bridge matching, TrigFlow, and the VAE compression analogy. This substantially changes the research positioning beyond citation-format edits.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten, and SDB is renamed ECSI. The stochasticity-control and score-reparameterization sections become a question-driven narrative about bridge paths, samplers and starting distributions. Background and related work are revised, core lemmas move into the appendices, and the appendix organization is substantially expanded.

P2.justification: v2 adds design-space diagrams, a characteristics table, ablation plots and new sample comparisons; redraws the base-distribution illustration; and restructures the main results into broader dataset and fixed-NFE tables. Retained material is also relocated: v1 Figure 1 becomes v2 Figure 9, and v1 Table 1 becomes the revised Table 8. Several appendix image grids are reused unchanged, while the document's typography and layout are reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for central contributions that v1 introduced with limited direct validation. Appendix A tests AFD under controlled diversity changes, while Figure 4 and Appendix D test the sampler ingredients and noise-design choices. Matched-NFE diversity comparisons and additional restoration evidence make the main tradeoffs easier to assess. Some useful earlier comparison rows are lost, and parameter inconsistencies remain, including the different b values attached to the same reported result in Figures 5 and 20. These limitations constrain reproducibility but do not outweigh the substantial gain in empirical support.
